text:
Jamie (support): heads-up — acme-inc reported elevated p95/p99 on /v1/generate since ~16:02 UTC, started after a deploy. p95 jumped from ~600ms to 2.7s, p99 ~6s. They sent a sample request id=acme-req-9012.
ops-bot: alert: prod-cluster-a p95 > 1200ms for model redwood-7b in region us-west — triggered at 2026-03-16T16:10:12Z.
Alex (eng-runtime): looking. any correlation with KV cache misses? those usually explain sudden p95 spikes.
Jamie (support): customer said they had a burst of varied prefixes (many small prompt variations). Support log: "lots of different chat prefixes per user".
Priya (sre): can someone pull kv_cache.{hit,miss}.rate and prefix_cardinality for the model pool? I'll check node-level load.
Mateo (runtime): running quick query: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (pool)` shows a 6x increase on pool=redwood-7b-usw. prefix_cardinality telemetry shows 18M unique keys in last hour vs baseline 900k.
Li (oncall): that smells like cache key normalization bug — we had one where trailing whitespace + session id produced unique prefixes. any recent changes to key normalization?
Alex (eng-runtime): there was a small change in prefix hashing in the deploy (strip -> not-strip) to preserve whitespace for exact-match behavior. I pushed a PR yesterday: runtime/prefix_key.go#L72.
Mateo (runtime): repro steps I ran: send 1000 requests with minor trailing-space diffs and unique session tokens -> observed nearly 100% miss rate and kv cache fills then thrashes. sample log: ```WARN kv_cache: miss key="prompt:Hello \u0020" node=ip-10-2-3-4 pool=redwood-7b-usw```
Jamie (support): customer thread: "we didn't change inputs, just saw latency spike after your deploy" — matches change timing.
Priya (sre): mitigation: can we flip back to old normalization quickly? or patch to fold session ids out of prefix keys?
Alex (eng-runtime): quick rollback possible. two options: 1) revert prefix-hash change (fast) 2) add a normalization layer that strips session tokens from keys (safer long-term). rollback is lower blast radius.
Li (oncall): I'll schedule a rollback to the previous deploy on prod-cluster-a in 10 min if no objections. need a quick playbook entry: rollback + warmup script.
Mateo (runtime): if we rollback, we should also run a warmup job to refill cache for hot prefixes: warmup worker will replay top-100k prefixes from recent traffic to reduce p95 during heal. I can kick that off.
Alex (eng-runtime): also increase cache soft-limit temporarily to avoid eviction storm during warmup: `kv_cache.pool_size = pool_size * 1.5` for 30m.
Priya (sre): agree. also set a circuit-breaker on p99 to shed heavy requests to a fallback (lower throughput model) if backend latency > 2s for >1m. avoids user-facing 6s p99.
Jamie (support): telling customer: "we're rolling back a small prefix change and warming the cache. ETA ~30-45m; will follow up when p95 back to baseline." they replied :thumbsup:.
Li (oncall): rollback started at 2026-03-16T16:26:10Z. ops-bot: deploy-rollback job started (run id rr-7781).
ops-bot: deploy-rollback rr-7781 completed on prod-cluster-a at 2026-03-16T16:31:02Z.
Mateo (runtime): warmup job started — replaying top prefixes from recent 6h. initial kv_cache_miss rate dropping already: 5m-avg miss rate down from 12k/s -> 3.4k/s.
Alex (eng-runtime): monitoring p95: 16:40 p95=720ms, p99=1.8s. still above baseline but improving.
Priya (sre): nodes CPU steady; eviction rate dropping. looks like we avoided a long outage.
Jamie (support): customer confirms latency improving, will keep them updated.
Li (oncall): postmortem notes — root cause: unintended change to prefix key normalization (whitespace handling) increased cardinality and caused KV cache miss storm -> eviction thrash -> p95/p99 regressions.
Mateo (runtime): next steps: 1) revert was correct immediate mitigation. 2) create acceptance test that asserts prefix_cardinality delta < 3x on synthetic session variations. 3) add telemetry alert on prefix_cardinality and miss-rate ratio. 4) implement explicit session-token strip rule for prefix keys.
Alex (eng-runtime): I'll open follow-up tickets and link to PRs + rollbacks. assigning: ENG-8721 (normalize keys + tests) to Mateo, SRE-3419 (alerts + circuit-breaker) to Priya, DOCS-99 (runbook update) to Li.
Jamie (support): thanks all — customer happy so far. closing thread after follow-up tickets created. :white_check_mark:
